mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly below zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand with nascent housing recovery, which historically precedes a negative S&P 500 return over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
regime_hint: late-cycle demand slowdown with housing stabilization
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4.0% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which historically precede negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly below zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average by more than 1.5% signals contraction in manufacturing output, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA by > 1.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary pressure regime, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to anticipation of growth resilience.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly above zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) above 0.4% for four consecutive months signals strengthening household balance sheets, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month by > 0.4% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 30% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly above zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for two consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which historically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to expectations of wage growth and consumption.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly above zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 6-month averages signals a broad-based demand recovery, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly above zero at 95% confidence.
